checks: Read 709f4ee1b13a1688 §§2–4, (2)–(10). An extreme nonself barycentric relation on a line has support of size two. At 0 the right weights are 1/2 and 1/3; at 1 they are 2/3 and 1/2. With unit inner seeds the increasing demands are 2 at 1 and max(3,3,4)=4 at 2. Reversal gives the second array.

Consecutive differences of the max and sum arrays are respectively (−2,0,2) and (−1,0,1). Hence linearly interpolated radii are concave and positive on the stated e range. The two max fibers at the sources are their interval intersections, and the same holds at each sampled outer base. No identity between the nonsampled bodies is needed.

Both inner intervals are symmetric and identical, the outer intervals have equal lengths and are contained in them, and the four integer fibers agree with the lifted hull. The exact four-fiber formula gives global raw maximum r+2R at both inner centers, including pure-base orientations. It also gives raw maximum three before motion.

Independently checked every tilt-one cap by min(2r,max(0,r−t)) for each interval radius and its threshold t. The original outside endpoint contributes zero length, the other inner trace is a half interval, and one outer interval is full. Thus max and sum give raw maxima and selected masses 3−10e and 3−11e against totals 8−24e and 8−28e.

Cross multiplication gives −4e(1−4e) for the max-versus-sum comparison and −4e for the sum-versus-original comparison. Quotient-rule derivatives are −1/8 and −1/16; the unscaled first payments are 1 and 1/2.
